speechtext: It seems to me that there is no evidence that we are succeeding with this expenditure and with our quarantine regulations in keeping out the disease because the number of cases that occur seems to be quite as large during the current year as it was last year, so that there are more instead of less.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I do not think that is correct.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Aly statement is borne out by the report of the Ontario Bureau of Health. The minister stated the other night that the disease could not have been imported from the other side of the line because only two municipalities had applied to the Dominion government to pay the expenses in connection with it. That may be, but I know of two cases myself that Hon. Mr. FISHER.
were so imported, and I am quite sure that there were a great many more.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: If such cases have occurred it must be that the patients came from the United States before the disease w'as apparent on them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Since the minister made the statement in the House the other night, I have looked up the report, and I find that in almost every instance in Ontario the disease came from the other side of the line.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Has there been correspondence with the United States authorities with reference to this matter ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: AAre get regular reports from the authorities as to the disease in the different states along the border.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Is the disease as prevalent in the United States as it was twelve months ago ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I am informed that practically the condition is very much the same as it was last year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Are there any places where the disease is particularly virulent ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: AAre get weekly reports from the different states and they are on tile in the department, but I have not examined them sufficiently to answer the question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Has any of this additional expense been caused by the admission of diseased immigrants ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Not at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: AVhat provision is made to prevent unsound immigrants coming in ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
The quarantine officials see that the immigrants are not afflicted with what are called quarantinable contagious diseases. In addition to that the immigration authorities have power under a recent special Act to check the influx of immigrants who may be in any way diseased or undesirable. That Act is administered by the Department of the Interior.
AH'. REID (Grenville). Are immigrants afflicted with trachoma prevented from entering Canada ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I believe that trachoma, and favus are two diseases which are dealt with by the immigration authorities under this special Act ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I notice quite a serious statement in to-day's ' Globe,' which I will read for the information of the minister.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.

speechtext: The Disease is Spreading in Buffalo. Believed to Have Been Introduced by Foreigners Entering From Canada-One Man Arrested.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
, June 24.-Trachoma is epidemic in this city. According to the statement of an official of the United States Marine Hospital, over 100 cases of the disease have been found among the employees of the Lackawanna Steel & Iron Company. A large number of cases of trachoma have been treated by local physicians in almost every section of the city. It is believed that the disease was brought here by foreigners who came into the country by way of Canada. Joseph Skool, an Italian with a bad attack of the disease, has been placed under arrest. He came from Brantford, Ont. The disease often leads to total blindness.
I draw the attention of the minister to that because the Americans may try to send these people back by way of Buffalo.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Are these diseases dealt with by the Agriculture Department or by the Interior Department ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Trachoma is not held to be a quarantinable disease in any country in the world, and it is not dealt with by the officers of my department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Are there two medical staffs; oue in the Interior Department and one in the Agriculture Department ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How many officers in the Agriculture Department are detailed to look after the epidemic of small-pox.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: We have a number appointed temporarily all along the boundary line. I read the names the other night and they appear iu ' Hansard.'

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How do you draw a distinction between what diseases come under your department and what diseases come under the Interior Department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Certain diseases have been declared by the International Quarantine service of various countries to be diseases which are quarau-tinable. An International Congress of medical men is held and they decide on what are quarantinable diseases, and every country adopts that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Has that been the process in the United States ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, the quarantine regulations with reference to contagious diseases in the United States and Canada are the same.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What is the practice if one of the officers of the bon. gentleman's department finds a case for medical treatment which does not come under the quarantine diseases ? Does he keep his hands off the case or does he call for a medical officer from the Immigration Department ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: If my officers, on inspecting a ship coming from Europe, find no quarantinable or contagious diseases on board, they give the ship a clean bill of health and she passes to port. My officers examine all passengers, not recognizing any distinction between immigrants and others. When the ship comes to port, thte immigration officers through their medical officers make an inspection of the immigrants as to whether they are proper and suitable persons to come into this country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
What is the practice with regard to cases that may occur along the frontier.
The - MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE.
I do not think there is any medical examination of immigrants coming from the United States, though I cannot speak positively as to that. The diseases which I have mentioned, trachoma and favus, are diseases which I understand do not flourish on this continent and are very little known here, but come from the congested parts of the old land.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Iu case an immigrant comes to this country say from the United States, and in the interior of the country is found by some local physician to be suffering from disease, would it not be well if it were generally understood that the physician would be paid a small reward for notifying the government, so that the government could get the immigrant out of the country as soon as possible ? Otherwise a case of this kind might simply be treated by the local doctor, and might remain in the country, causing the spread of the disease. I think if an arrangement of that kind were made, and it were generally made known throughout the Dominion, it would have a good effect.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I will draw the attention of the Minister of the Interior to the hon. gentleman's suggestion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What objection would there be to having the hon. gentleman's officers examine for these cases of trachoma ? I do not see why two officers should be at one port when one would be sufficient. Any person having that disease is rejected by the United States officials every time, and I do not think we want them'in this country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
That is a question of practical administration. When a ship is detained at quarantine, all the passengers are detained. When the ship is free, the immigrants go ashore, where they can be handled by the immigration authorities better than my officers could

handle them at the quarantine station. The rule is, I think, that diseased persons are returned immediately to the old land.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: No, sometimes they are taken to the hospital and are treated, and if they recover, are allowed to go on. The immigration officials allowed 181 to remain in this country which were rejected by the American officials. It seems to me that any immigrant who is not fitted to become a citizen of the United States is not fitted to become a citizen of Canada, ii they reject them, I do not think we want them. Certainly, we are not so anxious to have population here that we are willing to take paupers, criminals, and people who are diseased in such a way that they are rejected by our neighbours.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: This would perhaps be more fitting in connection with the immigration item. I understand that while these diseases are not contagious, they are not dangerous to the whole community like small-pox and other quarau-tinable diseases. They are only carried by the use of towels, combs and similar things ; and under ordinary supervision and segregation are not dangerous to general health and, therefore, it is permissible to bring people suffering from these diseases to the piers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: The reason I suggested the means I did of locating disease was this. A few days ago, there were some Greeks landed in this country, I think at Halifax, and they were simply sent from one place to another. They were really the most disgraceful lot of people I ever saw in this country. The municipalities sent them from one to another in order to get rid of them. The township of Matilda in the county of Dundas sent them to the township of Ed-wardsburg, and they were left along the roadside. They had a few rough tents, were very badly clothed, and appeared to have disease among them. They tried to get over to the United States, but the United States authorities were watching them. The Edwards-burg people moved them to Prescott, where they camped a couple of weeks, then moved further west.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Were those immigrants referred to passed by the officers at the vessels' side when they landed in this country ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I do not know where they came from, but if they came from Quebec or the maritime provinces they must have been passed by the quarantine officers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There is no officer in Montreal in connection with the Interior Department. There is one at Quebec, Halifax and St. John.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I may inform the hon. gentleman that the immigrants are all landed at Quebec.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Has the hon. minister any reports respecting some 200 or 300 who were refused admission into North Dakota during March, and were turned back to Manitoba ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: That matter is entirely in the hands of the immigration officials in the Department of the Interior, and I have no cognizance of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Have you any medical officers there ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, but they would deal only with quar-antinable diseases and would not interfere with the others.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I understand that this increase of from $50,000 to some $00,000 is due to outbreaks of quarantinable diseases in the United States ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, entirely to small-pox.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I would infer that the department is hardly exercising sufficient vigilance with regard to trachoma. It appears that the American authorities will not allow people afflicted with this disease to cross their border. The fact that it is not a quarantinable disease makes it all the more serious, because these people are allowed to go around the country and mingle with others, and in that way the disease is communicated from one to the other. A dozen or so of them will use the same towel. Now is the time, before this disease has got a foothold in this country, when we should stamp it out by turning immigrants afflicted with it back, just as the Americans are doing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I shall be very glad to repeat to my hon. colleague the Minister of the Interior the views of the hon. gentleman.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
I see by the Auditor General's Report, on page D-92-3. that the hon. gentleman has not at all improved upon the purchasing of supplies for Grosse Isle. I see one account here for $2,922. in which the prices paid are preposterous. I find that nineteen barrels of coal oil are charged for at thirty-two cents per gallon, and $1.25 for each barrel besides. In the case of goods purchased by tender, coal oil was got for sixteen or seventeen cents per gallon, and there was no charge for the barrels. Here is a charge for twenty-five gallons of linseed oil at $1.25. when every body knows that it retails at eighty cents. Gillet's lye. twelve boxes at twenty cents, the retail value of which is ten cents. Wringers, the hon. gentleman pays $8 for, and the best manufactured wringer sells at $4 retail. Forty-eight boxes of matches are charged at $7.80, when ten cents a box is all they are worth. One thousand one hundred and

three and a half pounds of rope are charged at twenty cents, when it could be got anywhere at sixteen cents per pound. Why will the hon. gentleman persist in allowing his officers to pay these prices ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: 1 gave instructions to the officers at Grosse Isle to scrutinize the accounts submitted, and see that the charges were in every case according to the usual value of the goods. I have no reason to suppose that these instructions were not carried out, but the particular items the hon. gentleman has read were purchased last year, before I gave the instructions.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: This account runs up to the 30th of June last year, and it was in the winter when we dismissed the items last session. Here is an account for five flags at 850.55, and making and finishing eight yards of bunting, $35. Why are these flags required at Grosse Isle at a cost of $85 ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I confess I do not know the value of flags- I do not remember that I ever bought any. Of course, the price of a flag would depend upon its size and character of the material.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: The total expenditure for this quarantine station at Gross Isle is between $55,000 and $60,000. As about one-half is paid for salaries, this leaves about $30,000 for supplies. This is a large amount, and I would like to know whether the hon. minister advertises for tenders ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: According to the Auditor General's Report the amount spent on Grosse Isle station is $32,482.58.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I see that 1 included the expenditures at St. John and some other places. But, I suppose about half the expenditure would be for supplies. These supplies must be furnished every year, and must include large quantities of ordinary staple goods. Are these supplies purchased by tender after advertisements in newspa-piers, or after circulars sent to dealers in the locality, parties recommended by persons in the constituency ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: The supplies are purchased from people whose names are given to the officers there. The great bulk of the supplies are purchased in the city of Quebec, but some are procured in Montmagny, in which county Grosse Isle is situated.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
This system would naturally lead to high prices being charged. I would appeal to the hon. minister to follow the system'tliat is followed-or claimed to be-by some other departments, and ask for tenders, if it be only by sending out a form
of tender to a number of those in the trade. For my part, I believe that by advertising in the newspapers the department will secure the best results. When goods are purchased under the system spoken of by the hon. minister, the seller is apt to charge the government more than an ordinary purchaser would have to pay. Of course, the Auditor General requires the accounts to be certified as fair anil just. But the officer at the station naturally feels that he must accept the account. If lie objects from time to time to these accounts, the dealer from whom they are bought will probably go to the member for the constituency, and being probably a strong supporter, will cause the member to appeal to the minister. Therefore, if the officer wishes to retain his position, he has no alternative but to certify the accounts as fair and just. This would account for some of the prices cited by the bon. member for South Leeds (Mr. Taylor), which are certainly fifty per cent higher than a private purchaser would have to pay. If tenders were publicly called for, the government could buy their supplies at much cheaper rates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I appreciate what the hon. gentleman (Mr. Reid, Grenville) says. I can only say that last year when the question came up I instructed the officer to scrutinize these accounts and only to pass such as they could certify to be fair and reasonable. I have no reason to suppose that my instructions have not been carried out. I am not prepared to discuss the details in these accounts, to show whether they are reasonable or not, because I do not know the circumstances. But I can assure the hon. gentleman that no officer would be dismissed or in any way interfered with in my department-and I believe the same is true of every other department-for refusing to certify to an unreasonable account. And no political pressure or any other pressure would be allowed to interefere with an officer doing liis duty in that respect.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: But the hon. gentleman knows that 32 cents per gallon for coal oil by the barrel is simply outrageous.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It seems high.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Why should not the hon. gentleman call for tenders, when we find one account here for $2,900 and another for about $1,000 V Then turning to the next page 1 find that there are large accounts right through. I find a charge here of 6J cents per pound for sugar. Surely, if the hon. gentleman had called for tenders he could have bought the best granulated sugar for $3.75 per hundred, as did one of the boats that was supplied. And I find a charge of 14 cents per pound for soap.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: That must have been for carbolic disinfecting soap, or something of that kind. I find other soap at 5* cents and 5 cents per pound.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
This may have been carbolic disinfecting soap, but you do not buy it elsewhere at so high a price. And here in Mr. Lesperence's accounts is a charge for practically two barrels of sugar at GJ cents per pound. And so it goes all the way through. Surely the hon. gentleman did not carry out the promises he made last year. He tells us now that he simply instructed his officers to scrutinize these accounts. Rut why did he not advertise for tenders for these supplies ? There are a lot of standard articles required here that should have been tendered for. Grosse Isle requires these supplies year after year, and why should one or two parties be called upon to furnish these supplies ? The hon. minister, as I have said, might have got sugar at $3.7.1 per hundred and he could have got coal oil at 20 cents per gallon, instead of paying 32 cents per gallon as it is here with $1.25 for the barrel

a charge quite unknown to the trade. What officer will pass such an account as that ? The people of this country have entrusted the hon. minister with their money to handle it just as carefully as if it were his own. He would not purchase at these prices for his own use : why then should he pay such prices when spending the money with which the public have entrusted him ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: When the hon. gentleman was last year examining the charges, the physician of Grosse Isle stated that he had purchased sugar for his own use at exactly the same price as that charged the government, and 'could not get it cheaper. I cannot speak as to prices for I have never purchased goods in that neighbourhood. There are a number of articles in these accounts which it would be quite impossible to purchase by tender. There might be some items which might properly be purchased by tender, and it is worth consideration whether some such arrangement might not be organized.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How many officers have you down at Grosse Isle to whom you furnish uniforms ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Practically all of them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I see one item, overalls, twenty-eight sets at $4. That seems to be a very high price. An hon. gentlemen near me says seventy-five cents would be a big price.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
I think perhaps that is going to the other extreme, though I must say I never paid $4 myself for overalls. I do not know, Mr. TAYLOR.
however, what character these are, or what they are made of. They may be of some particular material to suit the officials down there.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How many officials are there ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There are two doctors, fifteen or seventeen men connected with the steamers and who also work on shore managing the machinery. There is also the hospital staff, five men and two women, and there are two policemen and a carter.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Is the carter uniformed too ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes. It was found long ago that where a large number of immigrants are landed it is important that the officials should be in uniform, so that they may impress the people as having authority over them. The whole staff has been maintained in uniform for many years, and I think it is a very good practice. The overalls would probably be an undress uniform.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Does the department furnish more than one suit a year ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Only one suit a year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I believe the Interior Department allows a pair of pants to their officers ; and you furnish overcoats, caps and everything of that kind.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I am informed they get just one suit a year. It is made to order.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I think you ought to lot the contract.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: In a sense it isl a contract, that is to say, the pr.ice was fixed years ago, and has been maintained ever since. It is the same price that has been paid ever since I have been in the office, and I do not know for how long before. While no tender was asked for, the cloth, and the price, and every detail were submitted when the contract was given. It is practically a contract, though it was never signed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: But why should you give such prices ? There are two suits at $35, three suits at $25, and so on. Those are better suits than a good many members of this House wear.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: But there is a lot of gold lace, and buttons, and things of that kind on these uniforms.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I see in the Auditor General's Report where eight yards of bunting are charged at $35.	[DOT]

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Did you ask for tenders for
these overalls ? The idea of paying $4 a

pair for overalls that any store in Ottawa or in the country would readily sell for fifty cents, or seventy-five cents a piece.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: We don't know that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It is time you did.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There are $987.29 paid for uniforms. That is enough to uniform a small army. What is the number of the staff uniformed ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: About thirty altogether.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Averaging about $30 a uniform, ladies and all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I think we are entitled to some better explanation as to the value of these overalls. That price seems to reach over-all the others. $4.75 for a pair of overalls-they must be made of silk.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It is a suit of overalls.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: A suit, I am informed, is worth about $1.50. Really, I think there ought to be a more close inspection of these accounts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: We do not know the material of which these overalls are made.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Out of that item of $170,000, what proportion is for supplies furnished ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: $90,000 of it is not for our organized quarantine stations at all, that leaves only $80,000 for the organized districts. Of that $90,000, practically none of it is for supplies, except perhaps a few vaccine points. In the organized districts there was an expenditure of $80,000 altogether. I would have to go over the books a little to get the particulars.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Just approximately.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: At Grosse Isle, which is the largest station, the supplies last year cost $7,500, out of a total of $32,000 which was spent that year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I see that pea-jackets are charged for at the rate of $14.25 each, which is an enormous price. We handle the best kind of pea-jackets, the most durable for men in the lumber business, and $4 to $5 is a good price for them. I think the hon. minister could get a much more reasonable price if he would take the trouble to ask for tenders, and it is only reasonable to ask him to do so when such immoderate prices are charged. There must be somebody getting a big rake-off out of it, and I think it is time the hon. minister put his foot down on such charges as these.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
I see at page D-92 of the Auditor General's Report a charge of
$80 made for 160 vaccine tubes by Ed. Gauv-reau, M.D., Quebec. Vaccine points are things that we get for ten cents a piece.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: These tubes contain ten vaccine tubes each. That makes the charge five cents a point.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What we understand by a tube is a small glass tube with just enough vaccine in it to vaccinate one person.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: This is a large tube and contains ten vaccine tubes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I see at page D-102 of the Auditor General's Report that 37,050 vaccine tubes are charged for at the rate of five cents each.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: These are points.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: They are called tubes, and the charge is made by Dr. Bell, in Regina, at five cents a tube.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, the charge is five cents a tube. These are single tubes for each individual who is vaccinated. The others are large tubes, which contain ten of these single tubes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It is most unfortunate that the report does not show it more definitely.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, the report of the Auditor General in that respect seems defective.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Or the minister's explanation ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: No.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Perhaps we had better move for the aeounts and have an inquiry.
Cattle quarantine and veterinary division, $100,000.
Mr. GILMOUlt. What is the occasion of the increase here ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Here again the explanation is somewhat similar to what it was in the last item. We asked for $70,000 last year and in the estimates for this current year. That $70,000 was expected to cover everything connected with the contagious diseases of animals' branch in my department and amongst others things the charges in regard to slaughtering hogs affected with hog cholera. Unfortunately, during the last year there has been a very great prevalence of hog cholera in certain parts of the country, and we have had to pay out extremely large sums on that account. The consequence was that I was obliged to come down the other day and ask for a supplementary vote of $50,000 to cover the unusual and extra expenses, so that, as a matter of fact,

this estimate instead of being an increase over this year is a decrease, inasmuch as I have had to expend $120,000 this year and I am only asking $100,000 for next year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: In regard to cattle inspection, I would like to ask the hon. minister if he is taking any extra precautions this year in regard to cattle coming from away down south ? I noticed that Inspector Perry, of the North-west Mounted Police, in his report last year stated that the inspection was very lax at that time, and I understand that the chief inspector, Dr. Rutherford, went out west in May of last year to make an inspection. I see that in his report he says that a new trade has arisen out there and that a large numbers of cattle are being imported from away down south, from Montana, Mexico, and south of the Texas quarantine fever line, and that it is necessary that an inspection of these cattle should take place. He stated that it would be necessary to employ additional officers in order to make an efficient inspection. I would like to ask the hon. minister if steps are being taken to meet that necessity ? I ventured to say in the House some time ago that cattle had come from the south into our country and I rather think they are still coming. There is direct testimony before us now that cattle do come from south of the Texas fever quarantine line into our country. They have come up this year by thousands and nearly one-half of them died as soon as they were unloaded. Large numbers of them were dead in the cars. They were found to be weak and sickly. I think it is very necessary that a most efficient inspection should be made of cattle coming in that way. It is said that they were merely brought there for the purpose of grazing and then taken back at the end of the season.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There may be a few instances of that, but they are very few. In consequence of the visit of Dr. Rutherford to that section of the country, special arrangements have been made to watch these cattle and they are obliged to be accompanied by a certificate from the United States authorities that they do not come from the district infected with Texas fever and that they are free from disease. In addition to that they are inspected at our frontier when they come in.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: At all points.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: At all points at which they enter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Does the minister say they do not come from Texas ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: '1 hey do not come from the infected parts of Texas. A portion of the northern part of Texas is north of the Texas fever line.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Dr. Rutherford says in his report that some of these cattle, particularly those from Mexico, were brought from south of the United States Texas fever quarantine line, and he says :
I deem it advisable to insist upon the production by all persons importing such cattle, of health certificates signed by officers of the United States Bureau of Animal Industries.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: These cattle are said to have come from Mexico, which is not in the United States.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: He says they came from south of the Texas fever line.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, but at the same time it is not part of the United States.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: That does not make any difference. I am not directing my words against the United States, particularly, but against cattle coming from any place which is infected with that disease.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: These cattle have first of all to pass through the gauntlet of the United States officers on the frontier between Mexico and the United States, and then they have to pass our officers on the border.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I have more faith in our own officials than I have in the others. I do not think that a health warrant from American officials away down about Texas would be very valuable. I prefer our own inspection.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: These are officers of the United States Bureau of Animal Industries, the head of which is at Washington, and I believe he keeps his officers up to doing efficient work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What is the meaning of ' veterinary divisions ' in the item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It includes everything in connection witli quarantine and witli dealing with cattle disease both on the frontier and in the country. On former occasions we had two or three votes for this purpose, but this year and last they have been included in one. For the last year or two we have been obliged to undertake a considerable amount of work in connection with the health of animals in the country.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What duties does Dr. Couture of Quebec perform ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: He attends to the cattle quarantine at L6vis. and he also does any veterinary service for the department in the neighbourhood of Quebec.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
You pay Dr. Couture $1,000 a year, and he draws besides $564.70, or nearly $2 a day for ferry fares and cab-

hire. You can cross tlie ferry at Levis for five cents.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Dr. Couture practices iu Quebec and lie has to cross to Levis and thence to the cattle quarantine, which is probably a mile from the ferry. He is obliged to visit the cattle quarantine every day and sometimes twice a day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Is Dr. Pethiek, of Prince Edward Island, a permanent officer ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Has lie discovered any tuberculosis in that province ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: For the last year or more we have not had any report of any cases of tuberculosis in Prince Edward Island.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Dr. Pethiek has $50 a month salary. What do you allow him in the way of cab-hire ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: He gets an allowance per day for horse-hire. I suppose that some days he spends four or five times what is allowed him, and other days he might not spend anything at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How much is the allowance ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Thirty-two dollars and fifty cents a month.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: You said that on some days lie spends three or four times his average allowance for each day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It is about $1.25 per day and I think that some days he might pay $4 or $5.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There is no such a thing ns anybody paying $4 or $5 a day for the hire of a horse. In Prince Edward Island you can get a horse a whole day for $1.25.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: You certainly could not get it up here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Has the bon. minister any information about the recent outbreak of hog cholera in Bruce ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I am informed that probably it .came from the county of Essex. I am informed that the cars that stopped there were loaded principally at Belle River and at Harrow in the county of Essex.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What means have been taken to stamp it out ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: The usual course was pursued of stamping out this disease. All hogs which were affected or were in contact with affected hogs, were slaughtered, the premises were disinfected and the place quarantined.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How many were slaughtered ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Three hundred.	,

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: In such cases do you pay any proportion of the cost ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes, of the diseased cattle, one-third, and of those in contact, three-fourths of their value.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How many outbreaks of hog cholera have occurred in Essex during the past year ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
I believe there is no hog cholera known in Essex at the present time. Without giving the figures as absolute, I am informed that there were probably twenty outbreaks in the county of Essex during the past year.
,Mr. SPROULE. Then it cannot be stamped out very well.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: 1 do not undertake to say that it is stamped out. The misfortune has been that we have not absolutely stamped it out. We may stamp out the disease and have none in a certain county to-day, and to-morrow we may have an outbreak which may cost us $1,000. It is a most persistent and insidious disease, and we have not been able to adopt any plan for stamping it out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: How do you account for it being more prevalent in Essex than in other counties ? ,

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: For one reason, I suppose that there are a great many hogs there. The disease lias been there a long time, and although we have periods when there is no disease in Essex, the germs may remain, so that under conditions that are favourable to it, the disease breaks out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Do you not think it unwise not to have the place quarantined, but to allow the disease to be spread over tiie country to localities where it lias not existed before ? I notice every little while that there is hog cholera in Essex. To allow hogs to be taken from there to other parts of the country is only to spread the disease.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
1 would not like to characterize that county in that way. As a matter of fact, this year there has been more hog cholera in Kent than in Essex. Speaking generally, I do not think the other outbreaks in the county this year have been traced to Essex. The hon. gentleman speaks about quarantining. We do quarantine any section where the disease is found. We have quarantined whole townships, and have sometimes had bitter complaints about preventing people shipping their hogs. We have not done that



except where we thought it absolutely necessary to prevent the spreading of the disease from the township to other parts of the country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Then the quarantining could not have been very successful, for the fact is that the disease was brought from that county and broke out in Bruce. In speaking of the district in question, we refer to both Essex and Kent. The fact that the disease is so prevalent there may be Rue to the nearness of the United States or to the kind of food.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: 1 do not think it is imported from the United States. As a matter of fact, very few hogs come in from the United States. In the old days, when more hogs were imported, perhaps that was why that part of the country became infected. At the present time I do not think that any hogs come from the United States. If they do, they are quarantined for five days at the frontier, which is more than the period of incubation of this disease. The disease breaks out occasionally without any reason that we can find out-not where they were quarantined, but some how or other it is carried to other parts of the country, where it breaks out, and we have a heavy bill for the slaughter of hogs.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What has been paid for the destruction of hogs during the last year, from this cause ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Up to the 19th of May, 10* months, $33,534.71.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
I am afraid we can scarcely hope to be entirely free from hog cholera in the west. There is a general belief there that much of this disease is brought in from the United States. Whether that belief is well founded or not, I am not in possession of information that will enable me to say. I will only state the case as it appears. We have three railway trunk lines running through that western country. In the summer season the railways stop their trains at these stations and turn the hose on the hogs and wash them. That is said to be a source of the disease. Then, it is said that it is carried by dogs going through the country. We have had a very difficult experience in the west with hog cholera. I am prepared to say, from my own experience, that very stringent measures are taken by the officers of the department to do away with it. In spite of that, and what is thought to be a burdensome quarantine, which lias apparently completely stamped it out, it breaks out again unexpectedly at some distance away. I have absolutely no more hope that you will get rid of hog cholera in the western part of Canada than you will get rid of small-pox for all time. In Hon. Mr. FISHER.
many parts of the country it is thought that there is a good deal of carelessness in this matter. We will find some cases where farmers are not willing to tell for the simple reason that they only get three-quarters of the value of their hogs that come in contact with the disease and a smaller sum where the hogs are diseased and have to be slaughtered, but notwithstanding all this, the people are on the alert and there is a strong feeling that the disease should not be allowed to get root in any locality.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Why not quarantine the locality infected with cholera ? There must be laxity somewhere when a carload from an infected locality can be brought to another section where there has never been hog Cholera. In the United States localities infected with the Texas fever are quarantined and no intercourse is allowed between stock from that locality and stock in other places.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Surely the hon. gentleman would not propose to quarantine a locality ou mere suspicion ? It is only suspected that the cholera broke out in consequence of this carload of hogs being brought from Essex.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: The information I read was that the hogs were brought from Essex to feed on the whey and milk of the cheese factory and that it was among those hogs the cholera broke out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: It was not known at the time that there was any 'hog cholera in Essex county, and I would not like to quarantine a locality which was free from the disease. Essex county was free from the disease, as far as anybody could make out, when that shipment went from there to Huron. The disease was attributed to the shipment, but there was no disease in Essex at the time, nor was there any among the animals when they arrived at their new quarters. It would not be advisable or practicable to quarantine counties affected by hog cholera and treat them as portions of the south are treated with regard to Texas fever.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I do not know why the hop. minister would not be justified iu doing so. If the history of the past shows that the cholera has broken out over and over again in a certain locality, that locality should be quarantined. England has quarantines, Canada and the United States* on account of pleuro pneumonia, and we would be only doing what other countries have regarded as wise and prudent.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I want to get a little further information about Doctor Pethick. He is engaged permanently. Is he allowed to engage in private practice ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Dr. Pethick is engaged at a salary of $000

per year, wbicli justifies us in calling on him to do work for the department at any time, either in Prince Edward Island or the mainland, but he is allowed to practice for himself when not occupied in the work of the department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: According to the Auditor General's Report, page D-110, his salary for twelve months at $50, amounted to $000. He was paid horse-liire 313 days at $1.25. He must have had a horse every day of the year. Then for hoard he was paid $149.50; ferries, $1.70; railway fares, $2.25; disinfectants, $15.50; horse-hire, again, $17.50; telegrams, 75 cents;, postage, $2; telephone, $2.75; two thermometers at $1.50; rent of telephone six months, $5; subscription to veterinary journal, $5. Total $1,195.22. Then when 1 turn to page D-100, 1 find there Dr. Pethick again, horse-hire, $2; railway and boat fare, $0.25; board, $15.75; rabbits, $2; cage, $1. What were these required for ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: For some inoculation experiments which Dr. Pethick was carrying on.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Is the hon. gentleman sure that they were not rabbits infected with tuberculosis, which required to be quarantined ? Telegrams, $3; telephone, 75 cents; postage, 50 cents; making in all over $2,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Not at all; only $1,200.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman is right. But he was employed at $50 per month and his expenses were exactly equal to his salary.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: A very considerable amount of this expenditure was incurred by Dr. Pethick in an investigation on the mainland at Pictou of cattle disease. He was sent over by my orders to make an investigation regarding that disease. I informed the hon. gentleman a few minutes ago that Mr. Pethick's work is not confined to the island altogether. These items are for expenditures as well as for salary.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There are only 313 working days in the year and he charges for 313 days' horse-hire.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I am informed that he has an arrangement for horse-hire at $1.25 per day. Sometimes he spends a great deal more, and sometimes nothing at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: What were the duties of Dr. Rutherford in England during last year ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
Dr. Rutherford was sent to England the year before last to test cattle which were being exported from England to Canada- test them with tuberculin. An arrangement was made at the request of the im-173*
porters of live stock to test them in England instead of at our quarantine here. And for two seasons that was carried out. Dr. Rutherford was there the first season and carried out the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Did he make a report to the department of the work done ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: Yes. Regularly.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I would like to say to the Minister of Agriculture and to the hon. gentleman (Hon. Mr. Fielding) who is leading the House that my hon. friend from Peel (Mr. Blain) wanted to bring up the cold storage question on this item. I would suggest that this item be disposed of and that we discuss the cold storage question on another item. The census is the only one left.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: I would like to say that when we do take up that discussion on the census item, I would like to discuss the two questions separately. I would like to discuss the questions arising under what are called Professor Robertson's votes, dispose of that and then discuss the census separately.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext: There may be some sup-piemen taries.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PURCHASE OF CATTLE FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
speechtext:
I do not know of any supplementaries in my department on these items.
Some resolutions reported.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.

speechtext: The MINISTER OF FINANCE (Hon. W. S. Fielding) moved the adjournment of the House.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.
speechtext: What business will be taken up to-morrow ?

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.
speechtext: I think the hon. Minister of Railways and Canals (Hon, Mr. Blair) is absent; but if he is in the House to-morrow we shall probably resume consideration of his Bill, and afterwards go into supply, taking up the supplementary estimates for the'current year, the items under the direction of the Minister of Public Works. If the Minister of Railways and Canals returns, he may desire to take up a portion of the day on his Bill.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.
speechtext: It would be better to go into supply first, and let the Minister of Railways and Canals take the latter part of the day. He has been taking the earlier part of the day hitherto.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.
speechtext: If the hon. gentleman will promise me that when the proposal to go into supply is made we shall immediately go into supply, I will make a bargain with him.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY

speechtext: COMPANY.	.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: That the petition of the Nicola, Kamloops and Similkameen Coal and Railway Company presented to-day praying for an Act to confirm their charter be read and received forthwith, in accordance with the recommendation contained in the 14th report of the Select Standing Committee on Standing Orders.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: This is an exceptional time to bring up such a matter.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: It can come up on ' motions ' to-morrow.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: But the Committee on Standing Orders meets to-morrow and my reason for bringing the matter up now is that I wish it to be dealt with to-morrow and reported on. I spoke to Mr. Speakei' with regard to it.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: I have only to say that there should be some time when finality is reached with regard to these petitions. The rules are plain enough and are available for everyone who wishes to learn what they are. We met on the 12th of March, and it is now the 25th June. Yet these petitions are coming in as though this session were to go on perpetually. There should be some time when we reach finality with regard to these petitions.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: I may explain for the information of' the hon. gentleman (Mr. Sproule) that some weeks ago I obtained the usual permission from the House to present the petition notwithstanding the fact that the time has elapsed. The delay in presenting it has arisen in this way-the Act had to he confirmed hy the British Columbia government, because that company are asking in British Columbia for an extension of the time for the construction of their line, and there was delay until the Act was passed.

maintopic: NICOLA KAMLOOPS AND SIMILICA-MEEN COAL AND RAILWAY
speechtext: That would be an exceptional case.

Motion agreed to.
Motion to adjourn agreed to, and House adjourned at 1 a.m. Friday.
